messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High-severity - several containers restarted due to GPU OOM during prefill. Affected region: us-west-2. Pager notified. Logs: /var/log/containers/prefill*. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prefill-oom

alice-sre: saw a burst of very long prefill requests from a single route, caused prefill memory spike and OOM kills. Node kube-node-23 had 3 restarts in 6m.

bob-ml: likely long-context customer (customer_id=acct_9z) hitting 512k token-like path; model is running 16GB vram profile with no aggressive kv eviction.

carol-oncall: taking pager. @alice-sre can you confirm whether autoscaler kicked? I'll coordinate customer comms, paging escalation if we see error rate > 5% for 10m.

alice-sre: autoscaler didn't trigger — prefills happen inside containers so pod stays alive until OOM. Stack traces show OOMKilled from kernel:
```
[ 1234.567890] Out of memory: Kill process 4123 (python) score 987 or sacrifice child
[ 1234.567892] Killed process 4123 (python) total-vm:34567812kB, anon-rss:16384000kB
```
We also have CUDA driver warnings right before restart: `E CudaMalloc failed: out of memory`.

infra-bot: temporarily drained node kube-node-23 and cordoned it to stop noisy restarts. New pods scheduled to kube-node-27/28. :white_check_mark:

dan-support: customers reporting 503s and timeouts on generation endpoints ~15-40s. Which customers are impacted? I have one support thread from AcmeCorp.

alice-sre: metrics snapshot: 12:02-12:14 window: ~230 failed requests, error rate peaked at 7.8% on route `/v1/generate`. Top3 tenants by failure count: acct_9z (45%), acct_1k (22%), acct_zz (8%).

bob-ml: quick mitigation options: 1) enable per-request prefill token cap (e.g., max_prefill_tokens=16384) 2) fallback to a lower-vram model variant for long-context requests 3) enable KV eviction policy for this model family. I can push config if infra agrees.

carol-oncall: do it. I'll keep pager open. @eve-customer-success prepare a short customer-facing note: what happened, what we're doing, ETA for full resolution.

alice-sre: applying hotpatch to routing config to throttle prefill length for a few heavy tenants and enable cold-model fallback. Patch command used: 
```
# apply prefill cap
redwood routes update --route "/v1/generate" --prefill-cap 16384 --fallback-model redwood/small-compat:1.2
```
Pushing now to canary pool (10% traffic).

infra-bot: canary applied to pool `canary-prefill-10pct` successfully. No immediate regressions.

alice-sre: also increased eviction aggressiveness: `kv_cache.eviction_threshold=0.6` and restarted affected pods one-by-one. Restart command: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/prefill-worker -n inference --selector=pool=canary-prefill-10pct`

dan-support: confirmed AcmeCorp reported reduced errors after ~3 minutes. Sending status update to support queue.

eve-customer-success: drafting message: "We experienced transient GPU OOMs impacting some long-context requests. We've applied a temporary cap on prefill length and enabled fallback to a lower-memory model for long requests. Customers should see normal behavior now; we're continuing to monitor and will follow up with root cause." Approving now.

bob-ml: note for follow-up: need model-side quantization profile and KV eviction testing to avoid recurrence. I'll create a ticket.

alice-sre: for postmortem: capture spike origin (tenant rate, payload sizes), why autoscaler didn't help, and why fallback path wasn't engaged earlier. Also add better early-warning metric: prefill_vram_usage_percent per pod.

carol-oncall: taking handoff at 12:30 -> @alice-sre you own mitigation completion. If error rate < 1% for 30m I'll close pager.

alice-sre: ack. Current error rate now 0.9% (12:22). Tracking for 30m.

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity -> mitigated, assigned -> alice-sre, runbook step -> postmortem. Incident link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-179200

carol-oncall: thanks team. I'll keep monitoring and will escalate if we see new restarts. :thumbsup:

alice-sre: final note before handoff: saving debug bundle: `/var/tmp/incident-1792004321-debug.tgz` (logs, metrics dumps, core dumps). Uploading to S3 for postmortem analysis.

infra-bot: archived node kube-node-23 for forensic analysis.

carol-oncall: handoff complete at 12:37.
